issue: MCP HTTP transport fail-open when MCP_BEARER_TOKEN is empty
evidence: app.use('/mcp', (req, res, next) => { if (!token) return next() ... })
recommendation: Refuse to start HTTP transport when MCP_BEARER_TOKEN is empty unless NODE_ENV==='development'; require token length >=32. Exposed via Cloudflare tunnel this lets any internet caller invoke set_feature_state / adjust_traffic_rollout.
delta_status: residual after Stage2 fix-1 (Stage2 explicitly skipped this — see fix-1-feature-flag-store.md table row 'MCP HTTP refuse-start on empty bearer: No')

recommendation: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(provided), Buffer.from(expected)) with length pre-check. Combined with HIGH-1 above, an empty/short token plus timing-leakable compare is the auth surface for the whole HTTP MCP.

issue: writeFeatures() in MCP uses non-atomic writeFileSync — no tmp+rename like Express route has
owasp: A04 Insecure Design / A08 Data Integrity Failures
recommendation: Use the same tmp+rename pattern as backend/routes/featureFlagRoutes.js (or extract a shared store module — Stage2 explicitly deferred this). With three concurrent writers (Express PATCH + MCP-stdio + MCP-HTTP), a non-atomic write can leave features.json half-written and crash both readers (utils/featureFlag.js JSON.parse throws → auth/feature checks fail open or fail closed unpredictably).
delta_status: new vs Stage1 (Stage1 covered the Express side atomic write; the MCP side non-atomic write was not separately called out as a data-integrity finding)

issue: Traffic-bucket gating accepts client-controlled X-FF-Bucket header — attacker forces themselves into Testing slice
evidence: function parseBucketHeader(req) { const raw = req.headers['x-ff-bucket'] ... return Math.min(1, Math.max(0, v)) * 100 }
recommendation: A bucket value supplied by the client lets any user pick which slice of a Testing flag they fall in. If any flag in Testing mode controls security-relevant behavior (e.g. an unfinished auth flow, alt checkout, admin tool) the attacker can opt-in by sending X-FF-Bucket: 0.001. Derive bucket server-side from session id / user id hash, OR ignore the header and treat it as a debug-only override behind an admin gate.
delta_status: new vs Stage1 (utils/featureFlag.js was out of Stage1 scope)

issue: isFeatureEnabled falls back to Math.random() per call when bucket missing — same user gets non-deterministic flag state across requests
evidence: const effective = bucket !== null ? bucket : Math.random() * 100; return effective < flag.traffic_percentage
recommendation: Per-request Math.random means request N sees flag enabled, request N+1 sees it disabled. For any security-sensitive Testing flag this produces inconsistent authorization (e.g. user passes flag check on POST, fails on subsequent GET). Hash a stable identifier (userId or session) to a bucket and persist; never use Math.random for an authorization-adjacent decision.

issue: invalidateCache is exported but never called — backend flag cache goes stale across the three writers
evidence: function invalidateCache() { cachedFlags = null; cacheTimestamp = 0 } ... export { isFeatureEnabled, invalidateCache, parseBucketHeader }
recommendation: When Express PATCH (featureFlagRoutes.js) or MCP writes features.json, neither calls invalidateCache() on this util — backend feature checks can serve a stale answer for up to 5s. If a flag is used as an authz gate (Stage2's fix-2 already added one for order endpoint hardening) a freshly-disabled risky flag remains effectively enabled in this process for the cache TTL. Wire invalidateCache into the same fs.watch / shared store the Stage2 docs deferred.
delta_status: residual after Stage2 fix-1 — fix-1 added cache to featureFlagRoutes.js but did not unify with utils/featureFlag.js

issue: Session ID from client header used as raw object property accessor on transports{} — prototype-key DoS surface
evidence: const sessionId = req.headers['mcp-session-id']; ... if (sessionId && transports[sessionId]) { transport = transports[sessionId] }
recommendation: If sessionId is '__proto__' or 'constructor' the lookup resolves to Object.prototype / Function; subsequent transport.handleRequest is undefined and the request crashes the handler. Combined with HIGH-1 (no auth) this is an unauthenticated DoS toggle. Validate session id against /^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/ before lookup or use a Map.

issue: Filesystem path leaked back to client in error message
evidence: throw { error: 'FILE_READ_ERROR', message: `features.json not found at ${FEATURES_PATH}` }
recommendation: Both ENOENT and generic read errors echo the absolute path FEATURES_PATH back to the MCP client. Over the HTTP transport with no/weak auth (HIGH-1) this discloses internal filesystem layout of the container. Return a generic 'features.json unavailable' and log the path server-side only.
delta_status: new vs Stage1 (Stage1 looked at MCP auth but not at error-message leakage)

issue: search_project_docs accepts unbounded query length — embedding-cost DoS via Cohere
recommendation: z.string() has no max length. A 10 MB query will be sent to Cohere (paid API, multilingual-v3 charges per token) and to Qdrant. Cap with z.string().min(1).max(2000). Also rate-limit per session — RAG runs over stdio today but may be exposed over HTTP later (mirror of mcp-features).

issue: Upstream error messages from Cohere/Qdrant echoed verbatim plus internal QDRANT_URL leaked back to caller
evidence: message: `Qdrant search failed: ${err.message}. Check that Qdrant is running at ${process.env.QDRANT_URL || 'http://localhost:6333'}.`
recommendation: Echoing the Qdrant URL and raw Cohere/Qdrant error reveals internal hostnames/ports and SDK error structure. Log full error server-side; return a generic 'search backend unavailable' to the caller.

issue: Upstream fetch error message echoed verbatim in response
recommendation: fetch error messages can include resolved IPs / hostnames / TLS errors (e.g. 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.x.x:5678'). Even though the route is now admin-only after Stage2 fix-3, internal infrastructure should not be reflected. Return a generic 'upstream unavailable' with a request id; log full e.message server-side.
delta_status: residual after Stage2 fix-3 (fix-3 added auth but kept verbose error passthrough)

issue: Outbound URL built from N8N_WEBHOOK_URL with no host allowlist — SSRF defence-in-depth gap
recommendation: Stage2 fix-3 explicitly skipped 'Outbound URL host whitelist'. Today base is env-trusted, but the route trusts whatever ops sets — a misconfigured env var or compromised env file lets the backend POST to 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata) or internal services. Resolve N8N_WEBHOOK_URL host once at boot, store the expected host, and refuse any non-matching outbound. Pair with a non-redirecting fetch (axios `maxRedirects: 0`).
delta_status: residual after Stage2 fix-3 (skipped per task constraint, see fix-3-auth-and-integration-routes.md 'Skipped from synthesis recommendation')

issue: Client-side feature gating fully bypassable — sessionStorage bucket is user-editable
evidence: return isAdmin || getOrCreateTrafficBucket() < flag.traffic_percentage // bucket from sessionStorage which any user can edit in devtools
recommendation: useFeatureEnabled is the *only* gate in front of UI shown to non-admin users. A user opens devtools, runs `sessionStorage.setItem('ff_traffic_bucket','0')`, and is now inside any Testing slice >0%. This is acceptable for cosmetic flags but unsafe for any flag that toggles UI exposing unfinished/unaudited functionality (checkout v2, admin-lookalike screens). Document the threat model: 'client flags are UI hints only — every gated action MUST be re-checked server-side via backend/utils/featureFlag.js'. Today some screens may rely on the hook alone — audit each useFeatureEnabled call site.
delta_status: new vs Stage1 (frontend feature-flag layer out of Stage1 scope)

issue: Feature-flag mutations (set_feature_state, adjust_traffic_rollout) write file with no audit log
evidence: feature.status = state; feature.last_modified = today(); ... writeFeatures(features)  // no audit record of who/when/old→new
recommendation: MCP HTTP mode + weak bearer + no audit means a flag flip is forensically invisible — only last_modified date is updated, no actor/IP/before-value. Emit a JSONL audit line per write {ts, transport: 'stdio'|'http', actor: 'bearer:'+hash(token), feature_id, from: oldStatus, to: newStatus}. Required for the autopilot/n8n integration where flag changes can affect production.
